note: What the twins could not say, and what they could only say the long way round. A `declined` entry names a FORM the twin yields None for, and its example loses that form's coverage; a `friction` entry names a form the twin does reach, through a spelling the surface should not have needed. Both derive backlog, which is why they are one table. `row` is the ai-spec-execution.md row the fix lands on and `section` is the ai-python-first-revamp-discussion.md section that predicted it, or the correction where it did not.

entries.missing: ^ inside a compiled body, where the same ^ builds (xor ...) at the term door
entries.detail: OPERATOR_LOWERINGS maps __xor__ to the symbol xor, so S-term a ^ b is (xor a b); the same operator inside @m.define raises 'the operator BitXor has no MeTTa function. MeTTa has no bitwise operators'. The twin reaches xor as a free name instead, bound with m.fn so the Python stays valid. & and | diverge the same way and are the reason math_exp_random's equation lowers differently from its original.

entries.missing: MeTTa's (and ...) inside a compiled body
entries.detail: Python's `and` in a compiled body is Python's `and`: it lowers to (let* ((v A)) (if (py-truthy v) B v)), short-circuiting on truthiness. The original writes (and (<= $lo $x) (<= $x $hi)), MeTTa's own generate-and-test over two values. The operator that would mean it, &, is refused in a body. So the equation stored is not the equation the example stores, and the twin's extra inferences are that lowering.

entries.missing: a compiled body naming a hyphenated function it did not define
entries.detail: A body resolves a free name EXACTLY (the fallback from sqrt_math to sqrt-math was removed on purpose), and a body may name ITSELF in either spelling. So fib-tr compiles, and fib calling fib-tr does not: 'fib_tr is not a parameter of fib, not a function the engine knows'. The twin writes fib's equation at the container door instead, m += S["="](S.fib(V.n), S["fib-tr"](V.n, 0, 1)).

entries.missing: a lowercase symbol as data inside a compiled body
entries.detail: (= (spin $n) (if (> $n 0) (spin (- $n 1)) done)) answers the SYMBOL done. In a compiled body a capitalised free name becomes a constructor and a lowercase one is resolved as a function, so `done` raises and `Done` would store the wrong atom. The twin writes spin at the container door. There is no attribute form either: S.done inside a body is an ast.Attribute, which the compiled subset has no case for.

entries.missing: a module name that resolves without an importing file
entries.detail: import! has no dedicated Python door, which the term builder covers: m.eval(S["import!"](S["&self"], S.fibsmart)) is a legal zero-string spelling. entries.detail: ast.Match has no lowering, so every `case` equation in the corpus is written at the container door. P14.4's row already names this as the single most Pythonic missing construct and pins the lowering (chained unify with guards, as-patterns, `case _` fallback). entries.missing: a destructuring assignment as a `let*` PATTERN binding
entries.detail: (= (f) (let* ((($f1 $c1 3) (1 2 $d1))) ($f1 $c1 $d1))) binds a three-element pattern against a three-element value, which Python spells `f1, c1, _ = 1, 2, d1`. _define_expression._name_of refuses a tuple target: 'a compiled body binds plain names; destructuring and attribute assignment have no let* form'. The one-spelling rule points at let* with a pattern on the left, which the form already supports.

entries.missing: a compiled `match()` whose space, pattern and template are PARAMETERS
entries.detail: _define_expression._match_call requires the space to be a literal string starting with & and reads the pattern as syntax through _PatternScope, so (= (match-single $space $pat $ret) (once (match $space $pat $ret))) has no compiled spelling: a definition that takes a query APART has to be written at the container door. control/cut and control/once are the same definition twice, and the shape is a common idiom rather than a corner.

entries.missing: `superpose` over a BOUND value in expression position
entries.detail: superpose(x) in a compiled body is (superpose ($x)), a superposition over ONE alternative that happens to be $x, because _define_expression._x_Call wraps the argument list. (superpose $x), the superposition OF $x, is reachable only in yield position (`yield from x`) or as a for-loop source. So (= (program2 $Y) (let $list ... (superpose $list))) and (= (TupleConcat $Ev1 $Ev2) (collapse (superpose ((superpose $Ev1) (superpose $Ev2))))) are written at the container door. P14.4's expression-position rule names superpose(...) as one of the two forms to surface; this is the argument shape it has to admit.

entries.missing: two stacked @m.define clauses of one name that fix no literal head, which raise IndexError instead of stacking or refusing
entries.section: correction to §9c's definitional decorator: its two shapes are not interchangeable, and the function shape CRASHES where it owes a refusal
entries.detail: DEFECT, not a missing spelling, found writing this twin and reproduced in three files. Minimal case: `@m.define(name='oc')\ndef oc1(a): return a` followed by `@m.define(name='oc')\ndef oc3(a, b, c): return a + (b + c)` raises `IndexError: list assignment index out of range` at _define_twins.replace_twin_clause. Root cause: _space_definitions._locate_clause answers a replacement index whenever an earlier clause has the SAME patterns (both `{}` here, since neither fixes a literal), and _store_clause then calls replace_twin_clause(dispatcher, that_index, ...) on `twin_dispatcher(fn)`, which is keyed by the PYTHON function name (`oc3`) and is therefore a fresh dispatcher with no clauses. Arity is not consulted, so two clauses of DIFFERENT arity under one name hit it as well. Two consequences: the crash, and the design underneath it, that a second patternless clause is located as a REDEFINITION of the first rather than an alternative beside it, which is P14.3's own note that stacked @define clauses cannot express non-exclusive equations on one head. curry (`overloaded-curry`, two arities), multicall (`mycalc`, two alternatives) and functionremoval/functionremovalspec (`f`, two alternatives) all take the @rules shape because of it. The fix is either to key the twin dispatcher by the METTA name so the clause list and the dispatcher agree, or to refuse the second clause with the sentence _validate_clause_order already writes for the other collisions.

entries.detail: A literal default is what makes stacked clauses stack (`def fib(n=0)` is the head pattern for that position), so two clauses that fix NOTHING have no `@m.define` spelling at all. Measured on 2026-08-22: rebinding one Python name under one MeTTa name stores only the LAST equation (`@m.define def gg(): return 1` then `def gg(): return 2` leaves `(= (gg) 2)` alone in the space), and two DIFFERENT Python functions carrying one `name=` raise `IndexError: list assignment index out of range` from `petta/_define_twins.py:229` `replace_twin_clause`, because `_space_definitions._store_clause` computes `replaced` against the per-name clause records while the dispatcher is the new function's own empty one. A generator define writes one equation with a superpose body rather than two equations, so it is not the same knowledge either. `@rules` IS the door and these twins now use it: it writes a clause set without deriving a first-match guard, which `examples/basics/time_and_pragmas.metta` needs for `bounded-factorial` and `examples/control/forall.metta`, `examples/control/metta4_streams.metta` and `examples/control/thin_forms.metta` need for their identical-head sets. What remains missing is only the COMPILED half: `@rules` takes built terms, so a clause set whose bodies want to be Python syntax has no door. The crash stands on its own as a defect. [tested: ai-tmp/probe4.py and ai-tmp/probe_rules.py on the p14-twins-f worktree; commit=ddaa528d0cc463d42efa5f86eb194fad77f860f8]

entries.missing: the metatype accessor inside a compiled body, where Python's own type(a) is the named spelling
entries.section: §9d the concept map: the Python CLASS of an atom to its metatype
entries.detail: The design authority settles the metatype naming by deletion: "Python's own builtin `type(a)` answers the METATYPE by construction (the four classes ARE the metatypes, P5.1)". Inside a compiled body that mapping is absent: `_define_expression._PYBUILTIN_CALLS` bridges len, abs, min, max, sum, sorted, pow, str, repr, round and range, and not `type`, so `(= (inspect-opaque $written) (get-metatype $written))` has no compiled spelling and falls to the general hyphenated-name friction. Adding `type` to that table would close this one equation and give the concept map its compiled half.

entries.missing: a definitional-decorator spelling for a program's own equation over a name the engine already answers
entries.detail: `@m.define(name="match-types")` refuses before it reads the body: "'match-types' is already a function this space answers (an engine builtin, an operation, or an equation): defining it would stack a clause onto it". The refusal is a good default, so the gap is a spelling for the deliberate case rather than a bug: types/matchtypes extends `match-types` and types/types_dependent extends `get-type`, both of which are programs teaching the engine something new about a name it already answers. entries.missing: a definition door a one-form example can afford inside the 10% band
entries.section: correction to the band's treatment of registration cost
entries.detail: `@m.define` pays a fixed registration cost that a one-form example cannot absorb. Re-measured 2026-08-22, min of three fresh processes each: examples/basics/identity.metta costs 2577 and its decorated twin 2878, past the band ceiling of 2835 by 43, so the twin stays at the container door; examples/control/empty.metta costs 2508 and its decorated twin 2745, a ratio of 1.0945, so that twin was LIFTED to the decorator in this wave. The two files differ by 43 inferences rather than by kind, which is a band question and not a surface one: the band prices authoring and running together, and a definition's registration is authoring. Both twins now carry the current numbers rather than the +1,561 rule of thumb wave one wrote, which no longer decides either case.

entries.missing: a compiled body that stores the equation the example stores, rather than one that only answers alike
entries.section: correction to what the twins lane proves
entries.detail: The lane compares ANSWERS up to alpha-equivalence and the SET OF HEADS a (= $head $body) match answers; it never compares the bodies, so a compiled body that lowers to a different equation than the example writes passes silently. Measured 2026-08-22 by dumping (= $h $b) from both sides in fresh processes and matching under alpha-equivalence (ai-tmp/equation_diff.py on the p14-twins-f worktree): SEVEN of the 69 examples in basics/, control/ and types/ store different equations, and only one of them, math_exp_random, had said so. Four lowerings account for all seven. (1) `==` and `!=` in a compiled body are `(py-eq a b)` and `(not (py-eq a b))`, the prelude's Python equality, where the originals write `(== a b)`: basics/factorial, basics/fibsmart, basics/xor and control/tests program3. The operator table calls `==` taken for exactly this reason and the method form `a.eq(b)` builds `(== a b)` at the TERM door, so what is missing is a body spelling, not a design decision. (2) A condition whose syntax is not boolean-valued wraps in `(py-truthy ...)`: basics/xor. (3) An assignment is a one-pair `let*` where the original writes `let`: control/eval and control/tests program1. (4) A generator body is a superposition of its yielded answers, so a single yielded form is wrapped in a ONE-element `(superpose (...))`: control/metta4_streams. That last one is a free elision, since a superposition over one alternative IS that alternative; the non-generator body `return superpose(k, counter(k + 1, n)) if k < n else empty()` stores the original's equation to the atom, and was measured doing so. All seven twins now say which of these they carry. The lane could catch the class by comparing stored bodies under alpha-equivalence as well as heads, which is what the measurement above does in forty lines. [measured: seven of 69 examples store equations that differ under alpha-equivalence; command=ai-tmp/equation_diff.py; fixture=the basics, control and types twins against their .metta originals in fresh processes; commit=ddaa528d0cc463d42efa5f86eb194fad77f860f8]

retired.missing: `yield from` a call whose nondeterminism is unknown without silently splicing or changing iterable semantics
retired.detail: CLOSED by the P14.4 ruling. A self-recursive call, including a function whose Python and MeTTa names differ through name=, and a registry-known many-answer operation delegate whole. Any other known engine call is ambiguous: direct delegation would change a deterministic function returning iterable data from many Python values into one expression answer, while wrapping the call in superpose splices its application children. The compiler now refuses that shape and names both exact remedies: `yield f(...)` delegates engine answers; binding the returned data and then `yield from values` iterates data. Runtime deferral was rejected because superpose cannot recover whether an expression is a call or returned data after evaluation. test_yield_from_a_call_delegates_only_when_nondeterminism_is_known pins self/name= delegation plus cross-space and deterministic-call refusal. The metta4_streams and take twins now use the corrected self-recursive `yield from` spelling.
